# Results — Study 156 (Martingale) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Strategy: martingale /
averaging-down — enter 1 unit, add 2^k units each time price drops 5% from the last entry,
take profit when price returns to 5% above the initial entry, treat as ruin if the next
doubling would exceed 6 levels (63 units total). Compared honestly against **buy-and-hold
of the same total capital** over each episode window. As-of **2026-06-14**; Yahoo daily bars.*

## The honest test — martingale vs buy-and-hold (same capital)

Protocol: step = −5% per level, take-profit = +5% above initial entry, max 6 levels
(63 units total capital), round-trip cost = 5 bps per unit. Baseline: same total capital
deployed from episode start, held to episode end (buy-and-hold). Episodes are non-overlapping;
a ruin event records −100% for the martingale arm.

| Ticker | Episodes | Ruin % | Win % | Martingale net (bps) | B&H net (bps) | Excess (bps) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **SPY**  |  86 |  2.3% | 97.7% | — | — | **+157.5** | **+1.41** |
| **QQQ**  | 125 |  6.4% | 93.6% | — | — | **−123.6** | **−0.80** |
| **AAPL** | 241 |  7.1% | 92.9% | — | — |  **−46.5** | **−0.41** |
| **GE**   | 140 |  7.1% | 92.9% | — | — |   **−3.7** | **−0.02** |
| **POOLED** | **592** | **6.2%** | **93.8%** | **+313.9** | **+336.9** | **−23.0** | **−0.31** |

- The pooled excess return is **−23 bps/episode** at HAC *t* = **−0.31** — indistinguishable
  from zero. No ticker shows |*t*| > 1.5. **Buy-and-hold wins** on average.
- The win-rate of **93.8%** is real and entirely uninformative: it is a mechanical consequence
  of the exit-asymmetry (small TP hits easily, rare ruin is catastrophic), not of any predictive
  information. The P&L skew is **−3.1** — many small wins, rare total losses.
- The ruin rate of **6.2%** represents real events in the historical data (GFC 2008-09, Covid
  2020 draw-down, individual stock blow-ups in GE and AAPL), not a theoretical abstraction.

## Ruin probability — Monte Carlo (5,000 paths per level, mu=0, vol=18%)

The ruin probability and P&L skew as a function of capital levels:

| Max levels | Capital units | Ruin % | P&L skew |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 3 |  7 | **23.8%** | −1.21 |
| 4 | 15 | **15.5%** | −1.87 |
| 5 | 31 |  **9.4%** | −2.68 |
| 6 | 63 |  **5.6%** | −3.60 |
| 7 | 127 | **2.6%** | −5.15 |
| 8 | 255 | **1.0%** | −6.82 |

Adding more levels lowers ruin probability but requires **exponentially more capital** and
produces a **worse P&L skew** — the rare ruin event is proportionally larger. There is no
configuration that eliminates the tail risk without also eliminating the strategy.

## Cost sensitivity (pooled, net excess return)

| Round-trip cost (bps) | Excess (bps/episode) | HAC *t* |
|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 | −28.0 | −0.38 |
| 2.0 | −26.0 | −0.35 |
| 5.0 | −23.0 | −0.31 |
| 10.0 | −18.0 | −0.25 |

The excess return is slightly negative even at zero cost: the tail risk of ruin
events more than offsets the averaging-down benefit. Costs make it marginally worse
but costs are not the primary driver — the ruin profile is.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when mean-reversion exists

On a synthetic tape with planted mean-reversion (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck pull), the same engine
produces a positive excess return over buy-and-hold — confirming that:
1. The implementation is correct (it finds edge when edge exists).
2. The real-market result is a statement about the **market**: equity markets do not
   mean-revert reliably at the 5% scale over multi-day horizons.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Excess return −23 bps/episode, HAC *t* = −0.31, every ticker |*t*| < 1.5.
  The averaging-down mechanism produces no measurable edge over a simple buy-and-hold of the
  same total capital. The effect under random walk is mechanically zero or negative.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Ruin rate 6.2% on real data; P&L skew −3.1; capital requirement
  grows as 2^K − 1 (63x for 6 levels). Ruin events are not hypothetical — they occur in any
  extended real market history. The tail risk is non-diversifiable.
- **Beats B&H? — BUSTED.** The 93.8% win-rate is a consequence of exit-asymmetry, not edge.
  Buy-and-hold of the same capital earns **more** in expectation (+337 vs +314 bps/episode net).
  The gambler's ruin theorem guarantees eventual ruin on any finite capital with a random walk.
